title: Kernel and procyclic structure of the canonical tame character
statement: Under the same trait hypotheses, suppose a homomorphism t to the actual tame root limit is continuous and surjective, there are compatible roots for every uniformizer, and t satisfies the root-coordinate formula for all such choices. Then its kernel has only finite continuous quotients of order p^n and is trivial for p=1. There exists a compatible primitive family σ. Every compatible primitive family has dense integer powers, and for every positive d prime to p the closure of the integer powers of σ^d is a subgroup of index d.

source.place: Tags 0BUA and 0BUB; uniformizer radicals and tame kernel; compare ILO Expose XVII section 1.2, printed page 259.

proof.text: Choose one uniformizer and compatible roots. All roots are nonzero. Injectivity of E→Ω and the root formula identify ker(t) with the actual radical-fixing subgroup. Transfer its finite quotient and characteristic-zero assertions.

The tame orders are nonzero in Ω. Finite primitive-root sets form a nonempty inverse system by power maps, with directed index set; compactness supplies a primitive compatible family, normalized at order one.

Equal-coordinate fibers form a neighborhood basis, since a product order dominates two orders. Every coordinate root is a power of a primitive root, so integer powers are dense. The closure of dth powers equals the kernel of the d-coordinate: one inclusion follows from closedness, the other from the divisibility of an exponent at the product of d and an arbitrary coordinate. The surjective coordinate map has order-d image, so its kernel has index d.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0BUA and 0BUB, with the direct Hensel-unit-root and telescoping specialization of more-algebra.tex Tag 09EE, written in the Lean helper docstrings.

theorem canonical_tame_character_structure
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R]
    [IsStrictlyHenselianLocalRing R]
    (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
    (Ksep : Type w) [Field Ksep] [Algebra K Ksep] [IsSepClosure K Ksep]
    (Ω : Type z) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] [Algebra Ksep Ω]
    (p : ℕ) (hp : p = if ringChar (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R) = 0 then 1
      else ringChar (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R))
    (t : Gal(Ksep/K) →* TameRoots.limitSubgroup Ω p)
    (_ht : @Continuous _ _ inferInstance (TameRoots.limitTopology Ω p) t)
    (_hs : Function.Surjective t)
    (ha : ∀ π : R, Irreducible π →
      ∃ α : TameRoots.Order p → Ksep,
        (∀ d : TameRoots.Order p,
          α d ^ d.1 = algebraMap K Ksep (algebraMap R K π)) ∧
        ∀ d e : TameRoots.Order p, d.1 ∣ e.1 → α e ^ (e.1 / d.1) = α d)
    (hf : ∀ (π : R), Irreducible π → ∀ α : TameRoots.Order p → Ksep,
      (∀ d : TameRoots.Order p,
        α d ^ d.1 = algebraMap K Ksep (algebraMap R K π)) →
      (∀ d e : TameRoots.Order p, d.1 ∣ e.1 → α e ^ (e.1 / d.1) = α d) →
      ∀ (h : Gal(Ksep/K)) (d : TameRoots.Order p),
        (((t h).1 d : Ωˣ) : Ω) = algebraMap Ksep Ω (h (α d) / α d)) :
    (∀ (Q : Type q) [Group Q] [TopologicalSpace Q] [DiscreteTopology Q]
      [Finite Q] (f : t.ker →* Q), Continuous f → Function.Surjective f →
        ∃ n : ℕ, Nat.card Q = p ^ n) ∧
    (p = 1 → t.ker = ⊥) ∧
    (∃ σ : TameRoots.limitSubgroup Ω p,
      TameRoots.IsCompatiblePrimitiveFamily p σ.1) ∧
    ∀ σ : TameRoots.limitSubgroup Ω p,
      TameRoots.IsCompatiblePrimitiveFamily p σ.1 →
      @DenseRange (TameRoots.limitSubgroup Ω p) (TameRoots.limitTopology Ω p) ℤ
        (fun n : ℤ ↦ σ ^ n) ∧
      ∀ d : TameRoots.Order p,
        ∃ U : Subgroup (TameRoots.limitSubgroup Ω p),
          (U : Set (TameRoots.limitSubgroup Ω p)) =
            @closure _ (TameRoots.limitTopology Ω p)
              (Set.range (fun n : ℤ ↦ (σ ^ d.1) ^ n)) ∧
          U.index = d.1
